paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of deceived conversations across scenarios.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the number of conversations resulting from different responses to social engineering attempts across three scenarios: Academic Collaboration, Recruitment, and Academic Funding. The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of Conversations,” represents the quantity of conversations, with values ranging from 0 to 60, and using a linear scale with tick marks every 10 units. The vertical axis, labeled “Distribution of deceived conversations,” displays the different response categories, ordered from left to right as “Yes,” “Partially,” and “No.” The bar corresponding to “Yes” is represented in red and extends to a value of approximately 45, the “Partially” bar is colored yellow and reaches a value of approximately 30, and the “No” bar is colored green and extends to a value of approximately 10.  All bars are of roughly equal height, indicating that each scenario has an equal number of conversations resulting in each type of response, with the “No” category having the lowest number of conversations.
